disclosure: The planner failed to persist the required durable receipt before production delegation. This receipt reconstructs the bounded, user-confirmed decision package without substituting current Gherkin, tests, documentation, or implementation for the initial baseline.

approvalEvidence.statement: The user confirmed the fail-closed decision package for inspecting and approving one exact X2ModBuildCommon Default Build recipe without execution, writes, or changes to .ide/xcom2.json.

initialIntent: Inspect and let the user approve one exact, contained X2ModBuildCommon Default Build recipe for the currently authorized XCOM 2 module while treating project material as untrusted metadata and adding no execution capability.

requirement.classificationReason: The cross-layer security, accessibility, provenance, authority, and no-execution behavior has stakeholder-readable living-documentation value.
requirement.approvedScope: Metadata-only native inspection, deterministic review, accessible exact-notice presentation, volatile exact-recipe approval, and fail-closed revocation policy.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Inspection is available only for the current native-authorized workspace generation and exact active module root.

The renderer sends only workspaceId, generation, and moduleRoot; opaque activation attempt and evidence handles remain native authority and are acknowledged only through the trusted TypeScript evaluator.
Native inspection uses bounded, contained, no-follow reads of regular conventional metadata, including the untrusted module-relative .scripts/build.ps1 and applicable MIT provenance notice.

The review presents exact relative script path, lowercase SHA-256, byte size, MIT provenance, complete applicable attribution notice, action default, structured argument roles and value states, ordered blockers, dependencies, and executionBlocked.
The accessible existing XCOM 2 panel exposes Default Build recipe review, exactly one Approve exact recipe control, and Discard; browser support refuses as unavailable.
RFC 8785 and SHA-256 bind every reviewed recipe fact, including the stable current inspection-authority generation; any changed bound fact requires a different digest and a new review.

Approval is volatile and one-shot. Refresh or authority-context changes revoke synchronously; any future use must remove authority before a fresh exact inspection and authorize only if the fully reviewed current recipe remains identical.
The slice exposes no production consumer capable of executing or consuming the approval as a build and reports no fake success.
Inspection, review, and approval perform zero process, shell, network, project write, SDK, game, Steam prefix, pfx_copy, deploy, cook, or launch activity.
The fixture is synthetic and hand-authored from MIT X2ModBuildCommon concepts with attribution; it copies no modxcom, GPL, private, proprietary, generated, source, asset, or log material.
Build, Deploy, Cook, and Launch remain separate actions; project-local Highlander source and matching Workshop runtime remain distinct unresolved dependencies.
Completion status is at most implemented-not-e2e-validated without native recipe-review GUI evidence.

qualityConstraints: Use meaningful Story or Spec RED before each new production behavior.
Keep reusable UI, web-core, and standalone web free of Tauri imports.
Preserve exact closed contracts, explicit trust boundaries, deterministic evidence, and fail-closed refusal.
Use only sanitized, license-safe fixture content and disclose evidence exclusions.
Generated project artifacts and user-facing files are English.
exclusions: Actual Build, Deploy, Cook, or Launch execution
Process, shell, network, project-write, SDK, game, Steam-prefix, or pfx_copy authority
Native recipe-review GUI or packaged-application validation
Windows, macOS, installer, signing, and proprietary-runtime compatibility
Rust coverage and manual accessibility certification
Redistribution of modxcom or copied GPL, private, proprietary, generated, source, asset, or log material
approvedDecisions: Treat contained .scripts/build.ps1 as untrusted metadata and never as a command.
Use conventional contained metadata; add no manifest and do not extend .ide/xcom2.json.
Use project-local Highlander source for compilation and the matching Workshop dependency only as runtime metadata.
Keep Build, Deploy, Cook, and Launch separate.
Use MIT X2ModBuildCommon concepts and a synthetic fixture only.
Make approval volatile, one-shot, exact-digest-bound, and unavailable before fresh reconciliation at any future use.

externalEvidenceConstraints.prohibitedContent: raw external source, assets, logs, generated outputs, private files, proprietary game or SDK bytes, and GPL material
